THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the appellant/Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 30.04.2016 passed in MVC No.7/2012 by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Sidlaghatta.
2.

The brief facts of the case are that on 20.07.2011 at about 1.30 p.m., the petitioner has come from Gownapalli to Chickballapur in the SVMS bus, when she was departing from the door of the said bus, at that time, the driver of the said bus moved the said bus in rash and negligent manner, as a result, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous as well as simple injuries.
Therefore, the claimant has filed the claim petition seeking compensation.

sentences.text: 3. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company and the learned counsel for the respondents and perused the records.

4. The Tribunal after considering the facts and circumstances and evidence on record, has awarded compensation of Rs.3,50,680/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, under the following heads:
SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  (IN.RS.)
 1. Injury, Pain and suffering 20,000-00  2. Medical and Misc. Expenses 25,000-00
3 . Loss of amenities of life 20,000-00  4. Loss of income 20,000-00  5. Loss of future earning 2,65,680-00  capacity  Total 3,50,680-00 5.
Being aggrieved by the lesser quantum of compensation, the present appeal is filed.

6. In the present case, from the evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant was aged about 59 years, working as a coolie, has suffered fracture of type 'A' Pilon fracture both bone with displaced and was treated with fluids, analgesics, antibiotics and close reduction of fracture was done and above knee, POP cast was applied.
7.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in holding 41.34% as functional disability affecting to the whole body, but the doctor has stated 41.34% of permanent partial disability towards the left lower limb only.
Therefore, obviously, the functional disability to be taken at 1/3rd of the permanent partial disability as stated by the doctor.

It is further submitted that the rate of interest granted by the Tribunal is also on the higher side,
therefore, prays to reduce the compensation amount and rate of interest.
8. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants justified that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal filed by the Appellant/Insurance Company.
9. Upon considering the nature of injuries sustained, disability sustained, avocation, the compensation granted under each head is to be modified.
Even though it is not urged by the Insurance company that, the percentage of disability held by the Tribunal is on the higher side, but challenging the quantum of compensation.
Therefore, when it is needed for modification of compensation awarded under each head, therefore, this Court modify the quantum of compensation under each head.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head 'Pain and Sufferings', which is on the lesser side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
11. The compensation of Rs.20,000/- awarded under the head 'Loss of Amenities' is on the lesser side and the same is enhanced to Rs.35,000/-.
12. The Tribunal has granted a sum of Rs.25,000/- under the head 'Medical Expenses'.

Even though the claimant has taken treatment in the Bowring Hospital, Bangalore, which is a Government hospital, but in reality and considering the practical aspect that all the medicines are not supplied by the Government hospital due to shortage of medicines and some medicines prescribed by the doctor are procured from outside, hence, the quantum of compensation awarded under the head 'Medical Expenses' is found to be correct.
13. The Tribunal has held the percentage of disability as 41.34% is not correct.
The doctor has stated that the said percentage to the left lower limb.
Therefore, the learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submitted that 1/3rd of the said disability is to be taken as disability to the whole body as stated by the doctor.
However, considering the avocation of the claimant as coolie and age of the claimant, 20% of functional disability is considered for computation of 'Loss of earning capacity due to disability'.
The accident was caused in the year 2011.
Therefore, the notional income of the claimant is to be taken as Rs.6,500/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The appropriate multiplier applicable is '9'.
Therefore, 'loss of earning capacity due to disability' is re-
assessed and quantified as Rs.1,40,400/- (Rs.6,500x20%x9x12).
14. The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head 'Loss of income during laid up period'.
Looking to the injuries suffered by the claimant, she must not have attended to her work as coolie for a period of 4 months.
Hence, a sum of Rs.26,000/- is awarded under the said head.
15. The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head 'Food, nourishment and Attendant charges'.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.25,000/- is granted under the said head.

16. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation :
 SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  (IN.RS.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00
2 . Food, nourishment and 25,000-00  attendant charges
3. Medical and misc. expenses 25,000-00  4. Loss of future income due to 1,40,400-00  disability  5. Loss of income during laid up 26,000-00  period  6. Loss of Amenities 35,000-00  Total 2,91,400-00

4 17. The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.3,50,680/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,91,400/-.
The rate of interest of 9% per annum granted by the Tribunal is scaled down to 6% per annum.
The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,91,400/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

18. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.7/2012 dated 30.04.2016 by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Sidlaghatta, is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.2,91,400/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
iii. Costs made easy.

iv. Ordered accordingly.
v. The amount in Tribunal is ordered to be transmitted  to the Tribunal.
vi.
The other observations and findings of the Tribunal  are kept in tact.
